label: Delimiter step (<DEL>), content-dependent
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires at the <DEL> step: about 87% of activation mass and 78% of active steps are at the delimiter, but only about half of delimiter steps cross the threshold. Whether and how strongly it fires depends on sequence content. Rate is higher when the first original token (= the first output) is h, z, b or f (about 2.1-2.4x lift) or when the sequence is shorter (L=3-4). I found no simple token rule that separates firing from non-firing delimiters. The remaining ~13% of mass is weak firing late in the original phase (t>=2, mostly the first occurrence of a token, e.g. v, a, c), which often ramps up just before <DEL>. Essentially never fires at t=0-1 or in the copy phase.
